bilingual.notes: Approved program courses required to include Native American/multicultural education. Standalone 'Bilingual Education' endorsement listed under World Languages on DEED's available-endorsements page; add-on pathway via approved program (4 AAC 12).

eld.notes: Standalone 'English as a Second Language' and 'English as a Foreign Language' endorsements remain offered. Approved-program completion is the only method to add grade levels; content-area exam passing scores required. DEED also lists a 'Statewide English as a Second Language Acquisition, Bilingual and Literacy Education (SLABEL)' umbrella endorsement; no separate adoption date located in current SEA pages.

history.title: Alaska Bilingual-Bicultural Education Act enacted (Ch. 137, SLA 1972)
history.description: Alaska's Bilingual-Bicultural Education Act, codified at AS 14.30.400, requires every district enrolling 8 or more students of limited English proficiency from the same primary language background to operate a bilingual-bicultural education program — among the lowest enrollment thresholds of any state mandate. Originally enacted in 1972 in response to litigation over the State's failure to serve Alaska Native students in their heritage languages (notably the Tobeluk v. Lind / Molly Hootch consent decree pipeline that opened village high schools), the statute remains on the books and is the legal foundation for DEED's bilingual/bicultural credentialing pathways and the Alaska Native language immersion programs the State funds today.

history.title: Alaska designates 20 Alaska Native languages as official languages of the State (HB 216)
history.description: Governor signed HB 216 (codified at AS 44.12.310) recognizing Iñupiaq, Siberian Yupik, Central Alaskan Yupʼik, Alutiiq, Unangax̂, Dena'ina, Deg Xinag, Holikachuk, Koyukon, Upper Kuskokwim, Gwichʼin, Lower Tanana, Upper Tanana, Tanacross, Hän, Ahtna, Eyak, Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian as official languages of Alaska alongside English. The act is symbolic — it does not require state government to publish in these languages — but it is the legal predicate for DEED's continued investment in Alaska Native language teacher endorsements and the 2024 Limited World Language Immersion certificate, and it is cited in subsequent Indigenous-language education-funding decisions.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of Alaska's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

history.title: Alaska adopts WIDA ELD Standards Framework 2020
history.description: On 2021-06-10 the Alaska State Board of Education adopted the WIDA English Language Development Standards Framework, 2020 Edition (K–12) as Alaska's English Language Proficiency standards, in use since the 2021-22 school year. Cements Alaska's WIDA Consortium membership and ACCESS for ELLs assessment use.

history.title: Alaska adopts Seal of Biliteracy (4 AAC 06.077)
history.description: Alaska State Board of Education adopted 4 AAC 06.077 establishing the Alaska State Seal of Biliteracy, recognizing graduating high school students who attain proficiency in English plus one or more world languages. Alaska was the 49th state to adopt a state Seal of Biliteracy.

history.title: Alaska Reads Act takes effect
history.description: The Alaska Reads Act (HB 114, 2022) takes effect, mandating evidence-based reading instruction in K-3 and authorizing the K-3 Teacher and K-3 Administrator endorsements. Not EL-specific but applies to ELL/ESL support teachers serving K-3 students.

history.title: Limited world language immersion teacher certificate regs effective
history.description: Regulations 4 AAC 12.388, 4 AAC 12.397, and 4 AAC 12.405 establishing a Limited world language immersion teacher certificate take effect (filed 2024-07-22; published Register 251, October 2024). Expands pathways for native-speaker world-language and bilingual immersion educators.

history.title: Alaska Reads Act K-3 endorsement requirement takes effect
history.description: Effective 2025-07-01 (no extension or grace period), all K-3 educators in Alaska — including new hires and including SPED and ELL/ESL support teachers — must hold the AK Reads Act K-3 Teacher endorsement before working in any K-3 classroom (AS 14.20.015(c); 4 AAC 12.305).
